text: My biggest advice to people is, oftentimes the analysis paralysis of dotting every eye, crossing every tee sometimes chokes you out of opportunities. When you find something that gives you energy, just jump in with both feet.
speaker: Sanchan Saxena
context: Lenny asks Sanchan for advice on how someone starting out could follow a similar trajectory to work at incredible companies like Instagram, Airbnb, and Coinbase. Sanchan reflects on his own career path, noting that he never had a detailed plan but instead stumbled upon opportunities. He emphasizes that over-planning can prevent people from seizing opportunities when they arise.
text_ko: 제일 드리고 싶은 조언은, 모든 걸 다 맞추려고 하다 보면 분석 마비(analysis paralysis)에 걸려 기회를 놓치는 경우가 많다는 거예요. 어떤 일이 나한테 에너지를 주고 해보고 싶다는 생각이 들면, 망설이지 말고 과감히 두 발로 뛰어들어요.
text_zh: 我给大家最重要的建议就是，有时候你把每个细节都分析得过于透彻，反而会错失良机。当你发现某个事情能让你充满干劲的时候，就别犹豫了，直接全身心投入进去。
text_es: Mi mejor consejo es que muchas veces el quedarse paralizado analizando cada detalle hasta el cansancio te hace perder oportunidades increíbles. Cuando encuentres algo que te llene de energía, lánzate de cabeza sin pensarlo tanto.
key_sentence: Analysis paralysis chokes you out of opportunities; jump in with both feet.

vocabulary.definition: A state of overthinking or excessive deliberation that prevents decision-making or action.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, analysis paralysis can hinder progress on projects or initiatives, as teams may become bogged down in details rather than moving forward with implementation.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase often carries a negative connotation, suggesting that excessive caution can lead to missed opportunities.

vocabulary.definition: Favorable circumstances or situations that present the potential for advancement or success.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, opportunities can refer to market openings, partnership possibilities, or new avenues for growth that organizations can capitalize on.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often implies a sense of urgency or the need for proactive engagement to take advantage of the situation.

text: You take little bets, you try them out. If they don't work out, you build rapid recovery and start to do something else. And that is the meta story connecting all the dots in my life, in all the career opportunities that I've had.
speaker: Sanchan Saxena
context: Sanchan continues explaining his career philosophy, referencing a book called 'Little Bets' that validated his approach to life. He describes how taking small risks and quickly recovering from failures has been the underlying theme throughout his career moves from aerospace engineering to startups to major tech companies.
text_ko: 작은 시도(little bets)를 해보고, 잘 안되면 빠른 회복(rapid recovery)을 마련해서 다른 걸 시도해요. 그게 제 인생과 모든 커리어 기회들을 잇는 메타 스토리(meta story)이에요.
text_zh: 你就是要小试牛刀，试着做一些小的尝试。如果不行的话，就赶紧调整过来，换个方向继续干。这其实就是我人生的主线，把我所有的职业机会都串起来的那条线。
text_es: Haces pequeñas apuestas, las pruebas. Si no funcionan, te recuperas rápido y empiezas a hacer otra cosa. Y esa es la historia que conecta todos los puntos de mi vida, en todas las oportunidades profesionales que he tenido.
key_sentence: Little bets and rapid recovery connect all the dots in my career.

vocabulary.definition: The ability to quickly return to a previous state or condition after experiencing a setback or failure.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, rapid recovery is crucial for maintaining momentum after a project fails or a market changes, allowing companies to pivot and adapt swiftly.
vocabulary.nuance: This term often implies not just bouncing back, but doing so in a way that minimizes disruption and maximizes learning from the experience.

vocabulary.definition: Possibilities for professional advancement or employment that align with an individual's skills and aspirations.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business, career opportunities often arise from networking, skill development, and organizational growth, providing pathways for employees to advance.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can carry a positive connotation, suggesting potential for growth, but may also imply competition among candidates.

text: My advice to people is go get a job which will make you the fastest learner in the field of product management. That is what will help you a lot. No course, no degree, none of those things will help.
speaker: Sanchan Saxena
context: Lenny asks for advice on getting into product management. Sanchan explains that product management requires learning both the art (intuition, community insights) and science (data, methodology) aspects. He emphasizes that formal education can't replace hands-on experience in learning product management skills.
text_ko: 제 조언은 프로덕트 매니지먼트(product management) 분야에서 가장 빨리 배우게 해줄 직업을 구하라는 거예요. 그게 정말 큰 도움이 돼요. 어떤 강좌나 학위 같은 건 별로 도움이 되지 않아요.
text_zh: 我的建议是：找一份能让你在产品管理(product management)这个领域学得最快的工作。那才是最有用的。任何课程、任何学位都帮不了你太多。
text_es: Mi consejo: busca un trabajo que te haga aprender lo más rápido posible en el campo de la gestión de producto (product management). Eso es lo que de verdad te va a ayudar. Ningún curso ni ningún título te va a servir.
key_sentence: No course, no degree, none of those things will help.
original_text: My advice to people is go get a job which will make you the fastest learner in the field of product management. That is what will help you a lot. No course, no degree, none of those things will help. The most important thing will be how quickly can you jump in, learn the auto product management.

vocabulary.definition: An individual who quickly grasps new concepts and skills, often adapting to new information or environments with ease.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, being the fastest learner is crucial for adapting to rapidly changing markets and technologies, allowing professionals to stay competitive and innovative.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase often implies not just speed, but also efficiency in understanding and applying knowledge, making it a compliment in professional settings.

vocabulary.definition: A specialized area within business that focuses on the development, marketing, and lifecycle management of products.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech companies, the field of product management is essential for aligning product development with market needs and ensuring successful product launches.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase conveys a sense of expertise and specialization, often used to denote a career path that requires both technical and managerial skills.

text: The way to think about this is let's say you want to get to a destination, whichever destination it is, you probably want to get on the faster ship. You don't want to get on a slower ship.
speaker: Sanchan Saxena
context: Lenny asks what people should look for when choosing a company to join to accelerate their learning and career. Sanchan uses a ship metaphor to explain how to think about company selection - you want to join companies that are moving quickly toward success because your career growth is tied to the company's trajectory.
text_ko: 이걸 이렇게 생각해보면, 가고 싶은 목적지가 어디든 보통은 더 빠른 배를 타고 싶어요. 느린 배를 타고 싶지는 않을 거예요.
text_zh: 可以这么想：比方说你要去某个目的地，不管是哪儿，你肯定会选更快的那艘船，没人会选慢船。
text_es: La forma de verlo es: imagina que quieres llegar a un destino, sea cual sea. Probablemente prefieras ir en el barco más rápido; no en uno más lento.
key_sentence: Choose the faster ship to reach your destination.
original_text: The way to think about this is let's say you want to get to a destination, whichever destination it is, you probably want to get on the faster ship. You don't want to get on a slower ship. That's one metaphor to use in your mind.

vocabulary.definition: A specific place or goal to which one is traveling or aiming to reach.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'destination' often refers to the ultimate objective of a project, strategy, or customer journey, emphasizing the importance of clear goals.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can carry both literal and figurative meanings, making it suitable for discussions about both physical locations and abstract goals.

text: What I found is that at Airbnb, I learned a bunch of different things. One, I learned how to build products where software is just one part of the product. Let me explain that a little bit. The product of Airbnb isn't the app.
speaker: Sanchan Saxena
context: Lenny asks where Sanchan learned the most in his career. Sanchan explains that Airbnb taught him the most, particularly how to build products that extend beyond software into real-world experiences. He distinguishes between pure software products and products where software enables a physical experience.
text_ko: 제가 알게 된 건 에어비앤비에서 정말 여러 가지를 배웠다는 거예요. 먼저, 소프트웨어(software)가 제품의 일부에 불과한 프로덕트(product)를 만드는 법을 배웠어요. 그걸 좀 더 설명해볼게요. 에어비앤비의 프로덕트(product)는 단순한 앱(app)이 아니에요.
text_zh: 我在 Airbnb 学到了很多东西。第一，我学会了怎么把软件（software）只当成产品的一部分来做。让我稍微解释一下：Airbnb 的产品不是那个 app（app）。
text_es: En Airbnb aprendí muchas cosas distintas. Primero, aprendí a crear productos en los que el software (software) es solo una pieza del conjunto. Déjame explicarlo un poco: el producto de Airbnb no es la aplicación (app).
key_sentence: The product of Airbnb isn't the app.
original_text: What I found is that at Airbnb, I learned a bunch of different things. One, I learned how to build products where software is just one part of the product. Let me explain that a little bit. The product of Airbnb isn't the app. It is a means to an end. The product of Airbnb is the memories you're going to create when you sit in that Airbnb beautiful house with your family, with your friends, and you're building those memories. That's the product. It's in real world.

vocabulary.definition: To create or develop items or services that fulfill specific customer needs or solve particular problems.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, 'building products' often involves a collaborative process that includes design, engineering, and user feedback to ensure market fit and functionality.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase emphasizes the active role of teams in the product development lifecycle, distinguishing it from merely selling or marketing existing products.

vocabulary.definition: A collection of instructions, data, or programs that enable a computer or device to perform specific tasks or functions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, software is a fundamental component of products, often serving as the backbone for applications and services that drive user engagement and business operations.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'software' typically refers to digital applications, it can also imply a broader ecosystem of tools and platforms that enhance user experience.

text: I felt like it all compressed into three years something that you will learn in 30. I definitely didn't think that is what happened, but that's what ended up happening.
speaker: Sanchan Saxena
context: Sanchan describes his learning experience at Airbnb, which included hypergrowth, scaling the product organization from 30-40 people to 200 people, and crisis management during COVID-19 when travel essentially stopped. He reflects on how these compressed experiences provided decades worth of learning in just three years.
text_ko: 모든 게 30년 동안 배워야 할 걸 3년에 다 압축된 느낌이었어요. 전혀 그렇게 될 줄은 몰랐는데, 결국 그렇게 됐어요.
text_zh: 感觉这三年把本来得花三十年才能学会的东西都压缩了。我当时根本没想到会这样，但最后真就是这样。
text_es: Tuve la sensación de que todo se condensó en tres años: aprendí en ese tiempo lo que normalmente llevaría 30 años. No pensé que fuera a ser así, pero al final fue justo eso.
key_sentence: Compressed into three years what you learn in 30; crazy, crazy times.
original_text: I felt like it all compressed into three years something that you will learn in 30. I definitely didn't think that is what happened, but that's what ended up happening. Luckily, everything worked out, and I'm happy to share what we did and how we navigated through that with the audience, but it was some crazy, crazy times, man.

vocabulary.definition: Compressed refers to something that has been reduced in size, volume, or duration, often resulting in a denser or more concentrated form.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, compressed timelines or processes can indicate a situation where tasks or learning experiences are significantly shortened, often leading to increased intensity and urgency.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'compressed' can imply efficiency, it may also suggest a lack of thoroughness or depth, making it important to consider the context in which it is used.

text: The real genius isn't to dot every eye, to cross every team before you get started. The real genius is, what do you do when shit goes wrong? And I believe rapid recovery is the key to success.
speaker: Sanchan Saxena
context: Sanchan shares lessons from navigating Airbnb through the COVID-19 crisis, when the company had to lay off 1,900 employees and revenue dropped to single digits of the previous year. He explains that success isn't about perfect planning but about how quickly you can adapt and recover when unexpected challenges arise.
text_ko: 진짜 영리한 사람은 시작하기 전에 모든 걸 다 완벽하게 해놓으려 하는 사람이 아니에요. 진짜 중요한 건 일이 엉망이 됐을 때 어떻게 대응하느냐예요. 저는 신속한 회복(rapid recovery)이 성공의 핵심이라고 믿어요.
text_zh: 真正的聪明不是在开始前把每个细节都弄得滴水不漏，而是在事情出岔子的时候你怎么应对。我相信，快速恢复才是成功的关键。
text_es: La verdadera genialidad no está en dejar todo impecable ni en revisar cada detalle antes de empezar. Está en saber qué hacer cuando las cosas se tuercen. Creo que recuperarse rápido es la clave del éxito.
key_sentence: The real genius is, what do you do when shit goes wrong?
original_text: The real genius isn't to dot every eye, to cross every team before you get started. The real genius is, what do you do when shit goes wrong? And I believe rapid recovery is the key to success. What you do, how quickly you can recover from failure becomes really important.

vocabulary.definition: The ability to quickly return to a normal state after experiencing a setback or disruption.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, rapid recovery is crucial for minimizing downtime and maintaining operational efficiency after unexpected challenges, such as market fluctuations or technical failures.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase often conveys a sense of agility and preparedness, suggesting that an organization is resilient and capable of bouncing back swiftly.

vocabulary.definition: A fundamental factor or element that is essential for achieving desired outcomes or goals.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and startups, identifying the key to success often involves recognizing critical strategies, resources, or practices that drive growth and profitability.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase implies that while there may be multiple factors contributing to success, there is one or a few that are particularly pivotal.
